subject: Discovery recap & MPA draft: LucidWorkX pilot priorities
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@lucidworkx.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Discovery — LucidWorkX pilot priorities

Hi Maya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have a single source of truth and can move to a Mutual Action Plan: 

Key pain points you called out:
- Inconsistent latency across batch vs. realtime endpoints (spikes during peak query traffic)
- High per-token inference costs on current provider for embeddings and reranking jobs
- Audit/compliance needs (SOC2 evidence, VPC network controls) for customer-facing search features

Goals for the pilot:
1) Validate stable sub-200ms median latency for 128-token reranking under realistic traffic (10 req/s steady, 40 req/s burst)
2) Reduce embedding cost per 1M records by at least 40% via batching/quantization and caching
3) Confirm ability to run in your VPC for production-sensitive customers

Stakeholders we identified:
- You / Maya (Search PM) — product/requirements owner
- Amit Rao (Head of ML) — model/accuracy gatekeeper
- Tom Keller (Procurement) — contracting and SSO/KMS questions
- Lauren Bishop (Customer Success) — pilot onboarding and KPIs

Proposed milestone summary (high level):
- Aug 18: Pilot kickoff (data access, test corpus ingest) — owner: LucidWorkX / Amit
- Aug 25: Baseline run + initial perf readout (latency/cost) — owner: Redwood / Ben
- Sep 8: Model tuning and quantization recommendations + second readout — owner: Redwood / Ben & LucidWorkX ML
- Sep 22: Business review + decision to proceed to procurement/contracting — owner: LucidWorkX execs + Tom

Open questions / asks for you: 
- Can Tom be looped in on contract/PO timing?
- Do you have a preferred SLA window / absolute latency SLO for the pilot beyond the sub-200ms median?
- Confirm who will handle KMS keys for the VPC deployment (LucidWorkX-managed or Redwood-managed key?).

I attached a short pilot scope spreadsheet and will draft an MPA for your review. If the milestones above look right, I can send a formal Mutual Action Plan (PDF) with owners/dates and a few optional fallbacks (hosted -> dedicated -> private) for procurement.

Thanks — talk soon.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachment: pilot-scope.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Maya Patel <maya@lucidworkx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tkeller@lucidworkx.com>, Amit Rao <amit@lucidworkx.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery — LucidWorkX pilot priorities

Thanks Ben — helpful summary and aligned on the priorities. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency SLO: sub-200ms median is good; for procurement approval we also need P95 target <= 500ms for the reranking path during normal traffic.
- Cost target: the 40% improvement target looks right as a threshold for ROI in our finance model.
- KMS: we prefer LucidWorkX-managed keys (we can share a key policy and the KMS owner).
- Procurement timing: Tom, can you share the typical PO lead time (weeks)? We ideally want signed terms in the Oct window.

Tom Keller (external): "We typically need 4-6 weeks after final terms. If there's an expedited PO process for pilots, we can target mid-Sept but would need the MPA and a draft SOW by Aug 20."

One additional ask — can you include a short data handling summary (where logs live, retention, and redaction options) in the MPA? Our security team will want to see it.

Look forward to the MPA.

— Maya
Senior Product Manager, LucidWorkX
maya@lucidworkx.com
